The Pro-Action Operator Γ
The feasibility of a bio-inspired regulatory harness for LLM agents
Patricio Julián Gerpe  ·  Universidad de Buenos Aires
Today, an LLM agent's activation—when to act, wait, defer, or escalate—is typically decided by external orchestrators rather than by the agent itself. We ask a different question: can the agent regulate its own activation? Γ models activation as an explicit internal state—not a bid for biological fidelity, not a reward maximizer, not a learning algorithm, but a compact, inspectable regulatory harness wrapped around the LLM's own policy. The goal is to make activation itself experimentally addressable rather than externally scheduled.
1  ·  The problem
Autonomous LLM agents are increasingly deployed in high-stakes settings (triage, financial advice, public deliberation). Activation — when/whether to act, wait, defer, or escalate — is usually decided outside the agent by an orchestrator whose control rules carry less complexity than their environmental setting.
Ashby's law: a regulator must match the variety of what it controls.
2  ·  The gap
Orchestration frameworks (ReAct, LangGraph, OpenClaw) externalize activation — a graph, supervisor, or task-backlog heartbeat decides when the model runs; the model only supplies content.
Internal-regulation approaches (homeostatic RL, active inference) move regulation inside, but give no compact operator with separately inspectable subsystems — and no context-engineering mechanism to translate the numeric state trajectory into semantic labels an LLM can read.
What's missing is a single, compact, testable operator in which those regulatory domains — attention, arousal, affect, deliberation — are explicit, coupled, separately inspectable state variables. That is the gap Γ occupies.
3  ·  The Pro-Action operator Γ
Idea in one line: a regulatory harness around the LLM policy (not a replacement) that maintains sensitive internal values within viable ranges depending on context — like living organisms keeping variables in homeostasis — enabling Benefit↔Cost regulation of actions instead of brute-force gain maximization.
Each of the six subsystems is a thermostat: a set-point x* it is pulled back toward by an elastic restoring term, plus a basal drift, quality-driven relief when an action reduces its deficit, and linear cross-coupling to the others.
xt+1 = xt − κ⊙(xt − x* + δpert(t)) + λ − α⊙gt + W xt
κ⊙(xt−x*) elastic restoring  ·  λ basal drift  ·  α⊙gt quality-driven relief  ·  W xt linear cross-coupling  ·  δpert round-10 perturbation

Coupled by a fixed, sparse, hand-designed linear matrix W; the biological names mark functional roles.

↩ Feedback to Controller — action-quality g ∈ [0,1]
Three axioms of agentic autonomy — the assumptions Γ makes explicit so they can be challenged, not buried in implementation (SMT / Z3-checked for mutual consistency):
A1 · Autonomy
πi = πi(δi(t))
The policy depends on internal state, not only on external routing.
A2 · Impulse
pi(t) = σ(D(δi(t)))
A regulatory deficit creates pressure to act.
A3 · Quality gate
Δδi = −αg, α > 0
An action is adaptive only insofar as it reduces the deficit that produced it.
4  ·  RSVI
Regulatory State Verbalized Interoception. Each round, the six values are written into the prompt with set-points and a low/high reading. The controller modulates, it does not mandate — the LLM may follow or override.
hormonal = 0.58 (sp 0.30; high = arousal) cognitive = 0.44 (sp 0.40; high = deliberation) p(C) = 0.43 ( >0.7 → cooperate ; <0.3 → defect ) → "You may follow or override p(C)."
Not a rule like "if stressed, defect" — regulatory state as context.
5  ·  The test — 920-cell IPD
Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma — chosen for its rich evidence on human behavior in repeated social interaction, a non-trivial setting for asking whether an agent differentiates its behavior across opponent types.

Providers: gpt-5-nano, claude-haiku-4-5, deepseek-v4-flash.
Opponents: TFT · GTFT · Grim · Random.
Main contrast: Full-Γ vs ReAct — same provider, seed, opponent grid & history; only regulatory-state injection differs.
6  ·  Findings — early evidence the direction is non-trivial
ConditionCoopCoop (Grim)Opp. range
Full-Γ0.7200.4950.386
ReAct0.8420.8250.103

Table reports means. Higher range = more opponent-differentiated.
(A) OPPONENT DIFFERENTIATION
Range 0.386 vs 0.103 (ReAct). Cooperation 0.83 with TFT/GTFT drops to 0.495 against Grim — the agent treats opponent history as consequential.
(B) MATCHED CONTRAST — STRONGEST EVIDENCE
Remove regulatory injection and differentiation collapses — range 0.386 vs 0.103, paired bootstrap Δ = 0.283 (95% CI [0.233, 0.329]; n = 30 blocks; p < 0.001). ReAct sees the SAME history yet stays flat → not just the LLM reading history.
(C) NOT A PERFORMANCE WIN
ReAct cooperates MORE on average. The point is architectural — regulatory state becomes an inspectable control surface enabling Benefit↔Cost regulation, not maximization. Early feasibility evidence for self-regulated agents — not the discovery of a novel optimization algorithm.
7  ·  Honest scope (open work)
  • We don't claim six subsystems are minimal — it's one instantiation, its partition prior informed by the neurophysiology literature; comparing other N-subsystem operators is open work.
  • The constants — including the coupling matrix W — were fixed by hand before evaluation; sensitivity analysis and whether other settings work as well is future work.
  • Whether the numbers or the word labels carry the effect is untested — the scrambled-label ablation runs came back corrupted, leaving lexical priming for further study.
  • No payoff claim: per-interaction traces weren't retained. The contribution is the feasibility of explicit self-regulation, not a better score.
  • Tested only in IPD — whether it generalizes beyond this task is open.
This is a scoped feasibility study with early-stage contributions. Establishing causal necessity and generalization needs follow-up experiments with matched controls.
★  ·  Takeaway
1 · Reframe. Treat activation as an endogenous, regulated internal process — not a scheduling decision made outside the agent. This names a structural gap in today's orchestration paradigm.
2 · Mechanism. Γ (a compact coupled thermostat) + RSVI expose regulatory state to the LLM as an inspectable, auditable control surface — without prescribing which action to take.
3 · Evidence. Across 920 IPD cells, Full-Γ shows opponent-differentiated behavior that survives a matched ReAct contrast. Not a better IPD player — a demonstration that activation can be made experimentally addressable.
